posters.title: YOU HAD TO BE THERE
posters.brief: Photorealistic candid editorial poster, bright outdoor afternoon on a simple backyard porch, airy sky blue, leafy green and white rather than moody orange. Brett on right wears the fitted white T-shirt and white sports watch from reference3, short swept/spiky hair; his head tilts back slightly in genuine delighted laughter, eyes crinkling and mouth naturally open, one hand to his chest. Sean left in navy T-shirt is laughing too but looking toward Brett, easy ordinary friendship. Waist-up lively asymmetric composition, natural sunlight, 50mm documentary look, sharp identifiable faces, realistic teeth and hands, no clutter. Two game controllers and a closed notebook rest to the edge of the bench, subtle. Exact top title "YOU HAD TO BE THERE"; exact footer "GO TEAM, BROTHER." No other words.

posters.title: DID YOU JUST SAY THAT?
posters.brief: A polished stylized 3D animated-comedy movie poster with tactile handcrafted stop-motion-like materials, expressive but faithfully recognizable faces. Brett right in black rectangular glasses and turquoise graphic T-shirt per reference3, short upright hair. He gives Sean an unmistakable raised-eyebrow sideways look, one brow high, lips slightly parted in amused disbelief, palm raised as if pausing an outrageous statement. Sean left looks theatrically innocent while unsuccessfully holding back a grin, controller in hand. Clean lavender, hot coral, aqua and cream color blocks, playful studio backdrop with one small theater curtain shape, close medium portraits dominant, expressive eye contact through clear lenses and no glare concealing eyes. Exact large title "DID YOU JUST SAY THAT?"; small footer "YES. UNFORTUNATELY." Witty friendly reaction, no speech bubbles or other text.

posters.title: IN THE ZONE
posters.brief: A sophisticated photorealistic modern music-and-technology editorial poster, cool cobalt, lilac monitor light and soft neutral white, no sepia. Brett right wears a black crewneck with longer wavy brown hair falling at his temples matching reference3. Eyebrows gently drawn, lips pressed in concentration, gaze aimed intensely at work just below frame, one finger hovering over a keyboard. Sean left holds marked script pages and leans in to study the same work, equally focused and respected. Main portraits quite close, natural thoughtful expressions, live-in-studio feeling with soft-focus microphone and headphones rather than a giant desk still life. Exact restrained top title "IN THE ZONE"; small footer "LET THE IDEA FINISH." Strong identity fidelity, fine skin texture, no readable screen content.

posters.title: NOT TODAY, BROTHER
posters.brief: An expressive black-and-white charcoal-and-ink graphic-novel poster with one restrained electric-yellow accent. Brett right wearing the dark gray knitted beanie and heather gray shirt from reference3, light moustache/chin stubble naturally preserved. He leans back with an unmistakable weary eye-roll, brows drawn and one palm covering only part of forehead without hiding his face; lips pursed in exasperation. Sean left sits beside him, similarly tired but giving a small understanding side-eye while holding an obviously disconnected charging cable. Their game screen in background is an absurdly oversized loading symbol, no readable text; both victims of the same mundane annoyance, neither blamed or mocked for distress. Angular sketch energy, close faces, real dignity and affection beneath irritation. Exact top title "NOT TODAY, BROTHER"; footer "THE UPDATE NEEDS ANOTHER UPDATE." No additional words.

posters.title: UP TO ABSOLUTELY NOTHING
posters.brief: A witty neon-noir illustrative comedy poster, magenta, midnight purple and cyan with vivid coral orange. Brett right in orange shirt and oversized black sunglasses per reference3, slightly messy wavy hair with lighter tips; he lowers the glasses a little to reveal his own recognizable light eyes and gives a one-sided mischievous smirk, eyebrow raised, knowingly looking at viewer. Sean left with dark swept-up hair leans in beside him with a conspiratorial grin, holding a plain delivery-order slip with no readable words. Behind them a pizza box and a ridiculously formal desk bell hint at their prank gifts, theatrical side lighting and elegant pulp-poster composition. Their energy is benign secret planning, no criminals, weapons, drugs or explicit content. Faces recognizable, playful dark humor based on mock innocence. Exact top title "UP TO ABSOLUTELY NOTHING"; footer "WHICH IS ALREADY TOO MUCH." No other readable text.

posters.title: ALL GOOD, MAN
posters.brief: An emotionally warm, carefully painted watercolor-and-gouache portrait poster, pale sage, dusty rose, ivory and soft morning sky. Brett right wears a plain tan hoodie, short natural curls and slightly wispy fringe following reference3; his face carries an unmistakable relieved exhale, softened eyes and a small sincere smile, shoulders dropping. Sean left offers an equally relaxed smile, seated beside Brett on a modest kitchen bench, both holding ordinary mugs after a conversation. No consoling hierarchy or forced tears. Hands natural, expressive faces dominate, gentle translucent brushwork and beautiful negative space, fresh airy palette rather than amber theater decor. Exact title "ALL GOOD, MAN"; small footer "WE CAN START AGAIN." No other readable text, no copied cartoon branding from reference hoodie.

Brett right in plain light gray T-shirt and simple brown backpack straps with short spiky hair per reference3, clearly exhilarated: huge genuine grin, bright open eyes, one hand lifted in celebration. Sean left throws his head slightly toward Brett with a delighted laugh and a simple fist raised at shoulder level. They stand outside a modest theater/studio doorway into daylight, celebrating one small good idea, no trophies or invented achieved success. Real likenesses translated into excellent bold graphic portraits; physically credible hands and normal physiques. Exact large title "BACK ON OUR BULLSHIT"; exact footer "GO FUCKIN' TEAM." Neither aggressive nor threatening.

posters.title: WHAT IF WE ACTUALLY DID IT?

Brett right wears black rectangular glasses and a navy crewneck as in reference3, short swept hair, light stubble if present in reference, gazes slightly upward with a thoughtful almost-smile, eyes alert and hopeful. Keep lenses clear and both actual faces recognizable.
